exposure._solve: SOLVED FOR THIS SCENE 2026-08-14, not ported. Measured on diag_topdown (9 km, whole-map coverage) with the SKY MASKED OUT by local-variance: terrain-only linear luma 0.4135 against the solver target 0.3201 for sunlit terrain at albedo 0.2675, giving -1.786 - log2(0.4135/0.3201) = -1.923. THREE DENOMINATORS WERE TRIED AND THEY DISAGREE BY 0.13 EV, which is why the masking matters: whole-frame including sky gives 0.3470 -> -1.902 (the frame is ~57% sky at 9 km, so that is a sky-weighted average); a 4 km all-terrain probe gives 0.3805 -> -2.035 but samples only the central massif, which is snow-biased against a map that is 21.56% snow. Only the masked whole-map figure matches the area-weighted albedo the solver assumes. CROSS-CHECK: /Game/Alpine s Lumen-corrected -1.897 was derived independently for this same terrain, material and lighting, and agrees to 0.026 EV. That is confirmation by re-derivation, NOT a port -- and note the AlpineLab_8129 case where porting -1.897 would have been wrong, because that is a different mountain.
exposure._solve_caveat: THE SOLVE IS APPROXIMATE AND THE RESIDUAL IS NOT SMALL. Applying -1.923 moved the measured terrain-only linear from 0.4134 to 0.3909, where linear scaling predicted 0.3760 and the target is 0.3201. IT CANNOT CONVERGE BY CONSTRUCTION: the decoded PNG is POST-TONEMAP and the solver target 0.3201 is a PRE-TONEMAP scene value, and the filmic curve is compressive in this range -- a 0.137 EV step yielded -5.4% where linear arithmetic says -9.1%. This limitation applies to every exposure check this project has made by decoding a screenshot, including /Game/Alpine s 0.3169-vs-0.3201 agreement, which is closer than the method can actually resolve. The value is therefore anchored on TWO things that do not share this flaw: the measured brightness ORDERING (this scene reads brighter than the -1.786 reference) and agreement to 0.026 EV with alpine s independently-derived -1.897 for the same terrain, material and lighting. Frames at -1.923 read sRGB mean 0.610 with 0.000% blown. A proper solve needs the pre-tonemap value, which a screenshot cannot give. OPEN.

grade._rule: white_temp = sun temperature + 1000 K. Sourced: Electric Dreams runs an uncorrected 6500 K sun against WB 5600; Dark Ruins runs WB 4800-5000 under a low warm sun. Both sit about 1000 K below their sun, meeting the scene halfway rather than neutralising it. THIS RECIPE'S SUN IS 7800 K, so the rule gives 8800 K -- OUTSIDE the 5500-6000 K the brief quotes, because the brief assumed a 4500-5000 K sun. The RULE is applied, not the brief's arithmetic; if 8800 K reads wrong the sun temperature is the thing to question, since 7800 K is itself high for a low alpine sun.
grade._quiet: grain 0, vignette 0, chromatic aberration 0 -- the bench COMPARES frames and every grade element is noise in that comparison. Bloom is FFT at 0.4 on the engine's default kernel, a quieter version of the Epic grades.
